sampled:
but it would be disastrous for U.S. finances, which have been put under severe strain in recent years by a budget deficit that topped $1 trillion.

"It would be a disaster to let the debt ceiling not be raised because it sends a really bad signal to investors," Minerd said. "It would be a disaster to let it default because it sends a really bad signal to investors. So it's a really bad situation."
If the debt ceiling is not raised in time, the government would have to start paying interest on the national debt again. The government would continue to make full payments on all other obligations, including Social Security retirement and disability benefits as well as interest on the debt. The cost of borrowing for the United States, already at record highs, would rise even higher.
If the debt ceiling is raised in time, interest rates on U.S. Treasurys could rise by as much as 1.5 percentage points, said Howard Silverblatt, senior index analyst at S&P Dow Jones Indices. Interest rates are already up slightly since the debt-limit debate began.
